title: MLB CBA negotiations timeline: MLBPA says league has 'wasted months of time' as Dec. 1 deadline nears - CBS Sports

body:
As the 2026 Major League Baseball offseason continues to unfold, something vitally important to the future of the sport quietly hums in the background: the ongoing negotiations over a new collective bargaining agreement. The collective bargaining agreement, or CBA  (or Basic Agreement, as it's known in a formal sense), is the negotiated accord between players and clubs -- i.e., the team owners and commissioner Rob Manfred, who represents their interests -- that governs the working relationship between the two parties, typically for a period of five years. It covers things as mundane as players' meal allowances and travel protocols and as vital as minimum salaries, the structure of free agency, revenue-sharing specifics, and roster sizes. Every CBA can be distilled down to a fight over money, or, more specifically, how the league's revenues will be divided between players and team owners. The first CBA covered the 1968 and 1969 seasons and was the first in professional sports history. That was the handiwork of Marvin Miller, the pioneering head of the Players Association (i.e., the players union) and belated Hall of Famer. It was Miller's organizing skills, foresight, and training as a union economist that allowed him to make the Players Association a viable and effective labor organization. Every CBA negotiation from 1972 through 1994-95 resulted in some form and scale of labor stoppage, whether a players' strike or an owner-implemented lockout. After the cancellation of the 1994 World Series because of the worst labor stoppage in the sport's history, a long run of peace followed. That peace lasted until the prior CBA negotiations, which resulted in a 99-day lockout forced by team owners and delayed the start of the 2022 season. 
        
            
                MLB's new CBA proposal would restrict free-agency contracts, raise minimum wage, but only with a salary cap
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The current CBA negotiations have been underway for some time, and not surprisingly, the two sides remain far apart on several key issues. The biggest fight will be over the owners' renewed desire to implement a salary cap, which the union continues to view as a non-starter. The push for a cap has less to do with the notions of competitive balance and more to do with the ownership's internal belief that being the only non-salary-capped league among the major North American sports is harming franchise values. The cap, though, is but one of many pressing issues on which players and owners must find congruity.
Moving forward, the process will be uncertain and rife with posturing and pointed public comments from both sides. The hope, though, is that a new CBA will be agreed to before the middle of March 2027, at which point there's a high risk of having the 2027 season delayed or even abbreviated. To keep you informed of the twists and turns along the way to a new CBA, we've provided a detailed timeline of negotiations. That timeline will illuminate the important and finer points of the talks and, along the way, explain the implications of the various proposals coming from each side. The hope, of course, is that all of it culminates in a timely agreement that permits a fully intact and on-time 2027 season. Now let's begin. Nov. 17, 2026: MLBPA head says 'We've wasted months of time'MLB Players Association executive director Bruce Meyer said MLB is not serious about preventing the lockout and has "wasted months of time" trying to court public opinion when the two sides could have been having substantive negotiations.
"At the end of the day, this is going to come down to the bargaining table," Meyer told the Boston Globe. "And we have been for months, since May, looking for a serious partner in negotiations, and the league has insisted since May that they won't negotiate over anything economic outside of our agreement to a salary cap. In that respect, we've wasted months of time when we could have been having a serious negotiation. So I'd say the more the league is focused on things other than bargaining with us in good faith, I would say that's counterproductive."  Meyer also said the MLBPA has put forth proposals intended to promote competitive balance and correct the game's revenue disparity, but the owners are focused on a salary cap to "increase their profits and franchise values." He added that the two sides have made progress on non-economic matters, such as drug testing and gambling policies.Nov. 3, 2026: MLB proposes phase-in period for salary cap/floorTo allow for a "smoother transition" to a salary cap/floor system, MLB proposed delaying its implementation until 2028. That would give teams time to prepare and get their payrolls in order, and allow for a full offseason heading into the system. The current competitive balance tax and revenue sharing system would remain in place in 2027.
"We recognize that clubs will need a full offseason to prepare to operate within the cap and floor system. Therefore, with this offseason already underway, we proposed today to begin the cap and floor system in 2028," MLB spokesman Glen Caplin said in a statement. "This proposal would allow a smoother transition into the cap and floor system."MLB also upped its salary cap/floor proposal to $258.3 million and $180.2 million, respectively. Back in June, the league proposed a $245.3 million cap and $171.2 million floor. It says it is willing to discuss further phase-in scenarios for a salary cap/floor system.Oct. 8, 2026: MLB proposes 154-game season, postseason changesIn its latest proposal, MLB proposed reducing the regular season from 162 games to 154 games, and adding a standard off day to every week. The league also proposed extending the Division Series from a best-of-five to a best-of-seven, and allowing higher seeded teams to select their opponents in the Wild Card Series and Division Series. As with every MLB proposal to date, the 154-game schedule and changes to the postseason format are contingent on the MLBPA accepting a salary car/floor system.
Sept. 28, 2026: A 60-game mark could be crucial in 2027If labor strife lops off 60 or more games from the 2027 MLB season, then the consequences could be significant. The Athletic recently reported that if the forthcoming lockout extends into late May or so and costs at least 60 games, then most of the league's national broadcast and streaming contracts would be extended for another year, through 2029. That's significant because commissioner Rob Manfred hopes to bundle and centralize team streaming rights and share those revenues equally, and the current timeline would theoretically allow that to happen at the same time the national contracts are up for renegotiation. Tacking on another year to those national contracts would push back the significant windfall that owners and the league are expecting from that new media rights structure. As such, this is a heavy incentive, at least on the league side, to not let any labor stoppage drag into June. Sept. 2, 2026: Anonymous poll of players shows unity -- but not unanimity -- against capA poll of current MLB players across the full spectrum of salaries and service time conducted by ESPN showed strong resistance to the payroll cap and floor being demanded by ownership and league and being put forth as a precondition to every proposed change from that side. An excerpt: How open are you to a salary cap?NL starting pitcher entering arbitration: Not open.NL infielder making eight figures annually: Zero. No chance.NL infielder on two-year contract: Zero. Absolute zero.NL pre-arbitration journeyman: From what I've been told, I don't think it's good for the game. I just don't know if I know all the pros and cons of it. But, from everything we've been told, it doesn't sound like it's a good thing.NL reliever on multiyear contract: With the right criteria, I'd be open to it.AL starting pitcher in arbitration: I don't want it. In '94, they canceled the World Series, so if those guys can miss over half a year and miss the World Series, I think we're fully prepared to hold out for sure.AL catcher entering arbitration: I need more information, but perhaps I would listen on it.That's mostly strong sentiment that aligns with the MLBPA position on the cap, but it's not ironclad. MLB in negotiations and its public statements is seeking to tap into any existing divide between, broadly speaking, lower-salaried players with not much service time and more tenured veterans in their higher-earning years. There is a bit of a schism there, but it would take a substantial one to shift, in any exploitable way, the union's long-standing opposition to a cap-and-floor system. The ESPN piece covers an array of CBA topics. With the two questions related to the proposed cap, the responses can be broken down as 16 in mostly firm opposition to a cap and five not necessarily in favor but open to further discussions and reflection. Aug. 27, 2026: MLB proposes changes to roster rules, free agencyMLB proposed a series of changes to current roster rules that, in a statement, the league says are aimed at "creating more stability in rosters, getting the best players to the  Major Leagues more quickly, and accelerating the pace of the offseason." Among the rule changes included in MLB's proposal are:Weekly rosters that are set each Monday. Only roster changes necessitated by injury, bereavement, paternity leave, trades, and waivers would be allowed after weekly rosters are set.Teams would be allowed to carry 14 pitchers on their 26-man roster. The current limit is 13.The 10-day (position players) and 15-day (pitchers) injured lists would be reduced to one week and two weeks, respectively. The 60-day injured list would be replaced with a 12-week injured list.Yearly optional assignments to the minors would be reduced from five to four. Currently, players can be called up and sent down only five times per season. After that, waivers are required.Move Rule 5 Draft eligibility up one year and allow players selected in the Rule 5 Draft to go to the minors. Currently, players selected in the Rule 5 Draft must remain on the MLB roster all season.Two separate "Quiet Periods" at the start and end of the offseason that limit free agent signings between the first day of the Winter Meetings and Dec. 21. Trades would still be allowed throughout the entire offseason. In a statement, MLBPA interim head Bruce Meyer said an "artificial free agency window ... would reduce player leverage and create a game of musical chairs pitting player vs. player."All the proposed roster rule changes are contingent on the MLB Players Association agreeing to a salary cap-and-floor system.July 21, 2026: MLBPA proposes changes to draftDuring a negotiating session with the league, the players' union puts forth its own proposed changes to the MLB Draft -- changes that are, in essence, a rejoinder to the drastic overhaul earlier put forward by MLB. Among the changes the MLBPA proposes are: Continued draft eligibility for high school and junior college players and expanded eligibility in the college ranks to include sophomores;Preserving the current 20-round draft format;An increase in the amount of money allotted toward draft signing bonuses;Continuing to award additional competitive balance draft picks to small-market and lower-revenue clubs;Rejecting proposed hard slot bonuses and continuing to allow draftees to negotiate their bonuses;Allowing lower revenue clubs to increase their signing bonus pool for the draft and implementing automatic pool increases for lower-revenue teams that qualify for postseason play;A reduction to the penalties levied against teams that exceed their draft bonus pool;Allowing the trading of draft picks among teams, with some as yet unnamed restrictions;Moving the draft back to June.Additionally, the union proposes increasing the money payable to draftees under the incentive bonus plan and eliminating, according to the MLBPA, "the current practice of clubs deducting certain bonuses from players' continuing education benefits."The timing of the draft has actually been a concern for front offices for years, since it was shifted later in the calendar to coincide with the All-Star break in 2021. Holding the draft in July crams both that and the trade deadline into just a few weeks and making it more difficult to allocate resources.July 14, 2026: The sparring continuesCommissioner Rob Manfred and interim union head Bruce Meyer each hold press conferences on the day of the All-Star Game in Philadelphia. "I think that I have an ownership group that is more united than any group in my entire time of baseball," Manfred says, referring at least obliquely to the league's push for a salary cap. "They are a group that believes in what I am arguing for.""The supposed stewards of the game have spent an inordinate amount of time trying to convince those same fans that they don't have hope or they shouldn't have hope or that the product that they're paying to consume in record numbers is somehow broken," Meyer says of MLB's efforts to highlight perceived competitive-balance issues in the face of increasing attendance and television ratings. "I think it's perverse."
July 1, 2026: Temporary roster size expansionThe MLBPA puts forth multiple proposals, many of them dealing with procedural matters for purposes of player health, safety, and wellness. They include: Expanding MLB active rosters from 26 to 28 (14 pitcher maximum) for the first 15 days of the regular season. Allowing for placement of players on the 60-day injured list as early as the November tender deadline.Reducing the number of permissible in-season optional assignments per player from five to three.Accelerating eligibility for the Rule 5 Draft and ensuring a Rule 5 Draft will be held in 2026 and each year of the next CBA.Providing MLB service time and salary protections to pitchers who are optioned to the minors over the All-Star break and or immediately after a game where they met certain performance thresholds.Enabling all players to access club-collected non-proprietary performance data and video.The union's latest proposal is a reminder of the breadth of CBA discussions. Most issues are not the big-ticket items like a salary cap or lack thereof or revenue sharing structure but instead are somewhat esoteric matters that strike most fans as mundane. To players and teams, though, they're important considerations and in some instances may even provide a foundation of common ground moving forward. June 25, 2026: Limited free-agency contractsMore face-to-face negotiations take place, and MLB proposes more changes to the free-agency system, among other asks. MLB's latest proposal includes the following, all of which depend upon the union's acceptance of a payroll cap:
A maximum contract length of five years for players who switch teams and a maximum of 15% of the cap with 5% increases every year of the contract;A maximum contract length of six years -- and a max of 16% of the cap -- for players who remain with their original team under a new "Cornerstone Player" provision;Based on the league's proposed cap figure for 2027, the maximum contract for a player switching teams is $202 million over five years and $265 million over six years for a player remaining with the same team;An increase in the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1 million for players with at least two years of MLB service time;An increase in the minimum salary to $900,000 for players with less than two years of MLB service time with the opportunity for a $100,000 bonus from the pre-arbitration bonus pool (already established);The elimination of deferred contracts;Acceptance of the union's proposal to allow free agency after five years of MLB service time instead of six for players age 30 or older;Acceptance of the union's proposal to do away with the qualifying offer system for free agents.MLB in a prior proposal called for a cap on team payrolls of $245.3 million starting in 2027 and a payroll floor of $171.2 million. The league issues a statement that reads in full: "The biggest issue baseball fans want solved to strengthen the game is fixing the payroll disparity that leaves too many fans without hope of their team competing for a World Series title. Every other major U.S. sport has tackled this problem, and every year more small market teams in those leagues have a chance to win. The salary cap and floor proposal levels the playing field, allowing us greater flexibility to address longstanding player priorities while sharing baseball revenue with the players 50/50."Today, in addition to proposing the largest ever increase in the minimum salary, earned by over half of MLB players, we accepted two landmark changes to free agency that have been in place for 50 years. We agreed to both the MLBPA's proposal to provide earlier access to free agency, and their proposal to eliminate the qualifying offer system, a provision players view as a drag on free agency. We also proposed to eliminate deferred compensation and to create a new 'Cornerstone Player' provision similar to the NBA's 'Bird Rights' to give every team a fair shot at retaining their fans' favorite star players."We will continue working with the MLBPA during the bargaining process to improve the game for teams, players and fans."The MLBPA responds: "After making a series of proposals to reduce player compensation by billions of dollars, eliminate fundamental rights with a salary cap, and destroy the amateur entry process, Major League Baseball and team owners are now attempting to distract from the true impact their plan would have on baseball. These misleading offers are designed to look like 'improvements' but are of little or no value, given they are expressly conditioned on agreement to the league's cap system which eliminates the free market, and ensures gains for one player only come at the expense of another. "The league also introduced a litany of additional restrictions on player rights — limiting salaries, contract length, performance, award, and signing bonuses. While MLB claims to be acting in the interest of fans, their proposals thus far are entirely consistent with owners' long-held goals: suppressing player salaries and maximizing club profits. "Owners' attempts to pit players against players are nothing new, but they've failed in the past and will fail again now, because PA members remain unified. We are committed to achieving a fair deal that protects the rights of all players, promotes competition, and leaves our game better for future generations."Lacking from the league's latest proposal, at least on the public-facing side, is any revisiting of the recent changes to the draft and any mention of prior proposed changes to the league's revenue-sharing system. 
During these same face-to-face sessions, the MLBPA proposes a ban on prop bets placed on individual players, ESPN reports. The idea is to preempt harrassment of players by gamblers. The proposed ban would extend to bets placed on individual player performance prior to and during any MLB game. The MLBPA also requested that players be permitted to engage in paid endorsements and sponsorships with sportsbooks and prediction markets. June 18, 2026: MLB proposes sweeping draft changesMLB and the MLBPA meet for face-to-face negotiations, and owners propose sweeping changes to the draft and also push for an international draft. As for the MLB Draft, formally known as the First-Year Player Draft, MLB pushes for the following changes:A reduction from 20 rounds to 12 rounds;A $200 million hard bonus system in which players are paid according to their draft position with no room to negotiate (teams have not spent $200 million or less in the draft since 2010);High school players would no longer be eligible for the domestic amateur draft, and college players would be draft-eligible at age 20."Over the last several years, college baseball has undergone a remarkable transformation," MLB says in a statement. "Expanded scholarships, NIL opportunities, revenue sharing and significant investments in facilities and player development have made college baseball an increasingly important pathway that is producing major league-ready talent at an accelerated rate. Today's top programs provide players with resources, competition and national exposure that were unimaginable a decade ago. Our proposal is designed to build on that momentum to benefit the game at the college, minor-league and major-league levels. By creating a draft system centered around college-aged players and making most college players eligible one year earlier, more players will benefit from both a college education and an elite development environment while reaching professional baseball -- and ultimately the major leagues -- more quickly. We believe these changes will strengthen college baseball and deepen fans' connection to the next generation of major league stars. We look forward to working with the MLBPA throughout the bargaining process to modernize the domestic amateur system in a way that benefits players, clubs, and fans." 
As for the international draft, MLB proposed making players outside of the U.S., Puerto Rico, and Canada (who are already included in the standard draft) subject to a similar system. The international draft would, as with the proposed changes to the MLB Draft, come with a $200 million bonus cap. At present, international amateurs may sign with any team under the international free agent system, although teams do have hard budget caps each year.The MLBPA also issues a statement in response to MLB's proposals:Today, MLB made another set of proposals that are flat out bad for baseball, ones that would cripple the next generation of players and damage the future of our game. They would, among other things:Eliminate over a billion dollars in player compensation from the international and domestic system over the next five years, with a $400 million reduction from 2026 to 2027 alone.Destroy fundamental player rights and remove talent from our sport by barring high school and junior college players (anyone under age 20) from the domestic draft.Abolish an entire year of international signings by delaying the first draft until at least September of 2027 (and as late as March of 2028), denying young international players the ability to start their professional careers.Players remain committed to bargaining in good faith and leaving baseball better than they found it -- the league's proposals fall woefully short.June 5, 2026: Trump supports a capU.S. President Donald J. Trump publicly supports MLB's efforts to implement a salary cap. "If you don't have a salary cap, you don't have a sport, because they can't help themselves," Trump says. "Football has a salary cap. They should have done it a long time ago."It's shocking, frankly, that they didn't put a cap on many years ago," he said, possibly referencing the 1994-95 strike. "They had a chance to do a cap, but they blew it."June 3, 2026: Manfred talks luxury taxSpeaking to reporters following the owners' quarterly meetings, Manfred addresses the luxury-tax system he and the owners seek to replace with a cap. "We have tried mightily over several rounds of bargaining to use a competitive balance (luxury) tax to address competitive concerns," Manfred says. "And sometimes you've got to admit you failed."We made a proposal on one set of topics. At the outset of negotiations, I went and said myself, 'We're open to whatever ideas people have, but we need a realistic framework that addresses the fans' concerns about competitive balance.' You just can't ignore that financial penalties have not gotten it done for us."June 1, 2026: MLBPA says cap is 'institutionalized collusion'In a call with reporters, MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer addresses the owners' proposals. "Using MLB's definition of revenue and player share as set forth in their proposal and their presentation to us, player share under their proposal would go down," Meyer says. "Player share for this season, 2026, is projected to be well over 50 percent, using, again MLB's definitions of revenues and what counts against player share."Had MLB's proposal been in place in 2026, players, we estimate, would lose over half a billion dollars."
Meyer also refers to a salary cap as "a form of institutionalized collusion.""Our salary cap-and-floor proposal addresses our fans' concerns by leveling the playing field while sharing baseball revenue with the players 50-50 like the other leagues," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin responded on behalf of the league. "Under our proposal, major-league players will receive more compensation in year one of the system than in 2026. We are ready to listen if the MLBPA wants to counter our proposal at the bargaining table."May 28, 2026: MLB's first proposalsMLB and the owners publicly announce their first formal CBA proposal. Chiefly, they propose: A salary cap, including benefits expenses, of $245.3 million for 2027;A salary floor, also including benefits expenses, of $171.2 million for 2027;A 50-50 revenue split between clubs and players;The centralization and equal sharing of all local revenues.Using competitive balance tax (CBT), or luxury tax, payrolls as a guide, since they include benefits expenses, nine teams at present would be above the proposed cap line, while 12 teams would be below the floor. However, as Craig Goldstein points out, the amount needed to get all these teams below or above the relevant payroll thresholds amounts to an $18.7 million loss in aggregate player salary overall. Another sticking point will be how league revenues are defined. Owners no doubt seek to carve out things like real estate developments surrounding ballparks and ownership stakes in regional sports. As well, MLB's working definition of league revenues includes many expense deductions. On another level, the fact that Manfred is able to persuade large-market, high-revenue clubs to agree to equal sharing of all local revenues is a notable development. However, such a concession by those large-market clubs may be contingent upon the implementation of a cap. Another sticking point is that the league proposes an escrow system, as is used in the NBA and the NHL. This would mean a percentage of player salaries is withheld. If revenues fall short of projections, some of that money in escrow goes back to the league. If revenues are higher than projected, that excess is shared with the players. The MLBPA opposes the escrow system on the grounds that it undermines the notion of guaranteed player salaries. May 27, 2026: MLBPA's first proposalsThe MLBPA makes an opening suite of proposals to the league, including:A "competitive integrity tax" levied against teams that don't spend a minimum amount on player payroll.An increase of the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1.5 million.An increase of the bottom Competitive Balance Tax (more commonly known as the luxury tax) threshold from $244 million to $300 million.Increased sharing of local-broadcast revenues among teams but less sharing of stadium game-day revenues (the latter to incentivize on-field success).Tens of millions in extra revenue sharing to go to low-revenue teams that make the postseason or have a winning record.Free agency after five or more years, rather than six, for players who are at least 30 years of age at the time.Expanded draft lottery. Penalties for teams that neglect to spend revenue-sharing payments on team payroll.Draft picks and other incentives for low-revenue clubs active in free agency. Elimination of the qualifying offer for outgoing free agents.Increased compensation for lower-revenue teams losing players to free agency."Today, the MLBPA (Major League Baseball Players Association) presented a comprehensive set of economic proposals designed to advance the rights and benefits of players at all levels," Meyer says in a statement released by the union. "Our goal is to preserve and improve baseball's market system, rewarding competition on and off the field. Additionally, the players' proposals provide increased revenue sharing initially guaranteeing every small market club a minimum of $240m in revenue every season. This enhanced revenue sharing includes added protections to ensure clubs prioritize winning over profiteering. Ultimately, our proposals are designed to build upon the incredible momentum and popularity of our sport world-wide.""We appreciate the union making a set of proposals and we look forward to continuing the bargaining process and working towards solving the competitive balance problem our fans are telling us needs to be addressed," Caplin says in a statement. "We understand their proposals are designed to benefit players. Unfortunately, they do not address and in fact exacerbate the competitive balance problem our fans are telling us we must address. The MLBPA's proposal would reduce the amount transferred to lower-revenue Clubs, weaken the Competitive Balance Tax, and lead to even more payroll disparity than exists today. For example, under the Union's proposal, the Dodgers would pay less in luxury tax payments, giving them an additional $70 million to spend on payroll."May 12, 2026: Negotiations beginNegotiations on a new CBA formally begin between teams and players. Among the key issues to be discussed will be the league's desire for a salary cap, drastic changes to the revenue sharing system, league expansion, possible further playoff expansion, and an international draft.Dec. 1, 2026The 2022-26 Basic Agreement is set to expire at 11:59 p.m. ET, at which point owners are expected to lock out the players in the absence of a new agreement.

        There were two ranked-on-ranked matchups in college basketball Tuesday. Both looked great on paper. Neither were competitive on the court.Final score: Illinois 99, Duke 78Final score: Tennessee 61, Michigan State 46I guess a top-15 team handling another top-15 team at home easily isn't too surprising given the nature of the sport and the way capacity crowds can influence things. It happens. But what happened to Duke on Tuesday was downright shocking.The Blue Devils were 8.5-point favorites at tip. But they lost by 21. At home.That makes Illinois the first team to beat Duke by at least 21 points at Cameron Indoor since North Carolina did it in 1989. The Illini also became the first visiting team to win at Cameron while starting three freshmen since North Carolina did it in 2007.And then there's Andrej Stojakovic.Did you see what he did?
The 6-foot-7 Illinois senior took 21 shots, made 14 of them and finished with 46 points and six rebounds in 34 minutes. In the process, Stojakovic broke the record for most points ever scored against Duke at Cameron Indoor Stadium.
        
            
                Changes are necessary at Duke after Illinois routs home Blue Devils behind Andrej Stojakovic's historic game
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
That he did it in a high-profile matchup between two Final Four contenders made it even more impressive. That he also did it in a blowout while Illinois was down two starters, including preseason All-American David Mirkovic, made it unforgettable.Illinois is up to No. 5 in Wednesday morning's updated CBS Sports Top 25 And 1 daily college basketball rankings. Duke is down to No. 14.And is it time to worry about the Blue Devils?This is the first year Duke coach Jon Scheyer hasn't had the eventual CBS Sports Player of the Year on his roster since the 2023-24 season. It's obviously not going well. The Blue Devils are 3-2 with three whatever-wins, a lopsided loss at home to an Illinois team that had already lost at Texas Tech, and another loss to a Michigan State team that just got routed by Tennessee. Duke's high-priced transfer, John Blackwell, is only averaging 9.0 points while shooting 31.3% from the field. As a team, the Blue Devils are only shooting 28.2% from 3-point range.
        
            
                College basketball winners, losers: Florida, Houston to clash in 2025 title game rematch; Duke pounded at home
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Needless to say, the talent that had Duke as the preseason favorite in the betting markets to win the 2027 NCAA Tournament remains in place, and it's not even Thanksgiving, so sell all Duke stock at your own risk. But, after five games, the questions about the Blue Devils seem bigger than most anticipated they'd be.

title: College football odds, picks, predictions: LSU-Tennessee, Michigan-UCLA lead Week 12 - CBS Sports
description: Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer reveal their picks for college football's biggest matchups of the weekend
body:
Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer reveal their picks for college football's biggest matchups of the weekend
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:00 am ET
                        
                •
            
            10 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Call college football's Week 12 schedule a breather if you want to -- just keep that same energy again Saturday night when there are a handful of results we never saw coming.There isn't a single AP Top 25 matchup on the schedule, but 10 ranked teams are single-digit favorites on the road. How many of them are you willing to trust with their College Football Playoff seeding and potential conference title hopes on the line?  This is the kind of slate that looks harmless until a favorite trails by a couple of touchdowns early or starts feeling the heat in the second half of a game that could go in either direction. We're picking the biggest games of Week 12, including a few where the road favorite might spend Sunday figuring out how much damage one afternoon did to its résumé.
Season results: Brad Crawford (67-34 straight up, 45-55-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (73-28 straight up, 50–50-1 ATS)We're in a futile state of affairs, folks. I'm afraid the hole is too deep for me to crawl out of this season to continue my winning streak against Hummer in our annual head-to-head picks battle. We both had losing records last week, but he still picked up a game on me and now holds a five-game lead with a couple of weekends left.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 14 Ohio State (-3.5) at NebraskaHummer (Ohio State -3.5): These are two good and flawed teams. Both are top 20 defenses. Both have largely struggled on offense since mid-October. An injury to Julian Sayin caused Ohio State's issues. Tougher competition caught up to the Huskers. I just don't see Nebraska moving the ball all that well against the Buckeyes. Luke Fahey has played pretty well the last two weeks. He and the Buckeyes' offense do enough. … Ohio State 27, Nebraska 21.
Crawford (Ohio State -3.5): Y'all know Matt Rhule's record against top-25 opponents, right? I can keep things short here if so. The Buckeyes still have an outside shot at getting in the CFP discussion as a bubble team with convincing wins this week and next (against Michigan). Jeremiah Smith needs a monster outing on the road to remain in the frontrunner discussion for the Heisman. He has scored in seven straight games but is no longer the first player voters think of when top players are mentioned. ... Ohio State 27, Nebraska 20.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 10 BYU (-6.5) at KansasHummer (BYU -6.5): Kansas is an odd team. The Jayhawks are top 45 nationally in both yards per play and yards allowed per play. But they're also just 2-5 in the Big 12 and have struggled with both turnovers and injuries. The problem for Kansas is that it can struggle to stop the run, and that's what BYU does best. I could see this being close. But I'll take the team with a lot on the line that's been incredibly consistent this season. … BYU 31, Kansas 24.Crawford (BYU -6.5): At 4-6 overall this season, the Jayhawks need consecutive wins over BYU and Oklahoma State to reach bowl eligibility. It's not going to come to fruition, unfortunately. BYU has to win and look good doing it to avoid dropping in the CFP rankings, and there's no margin for error in the conference title discussion behind Utah and Texas Tech. BYU does not control its own destiny, but if the Cougars win out, they're going to have a strong argument for inclusion. ... BYU 34, Kansas 20.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 15 Iowa (-6.5) at IllinoisHummer (Iowa -6.5): The Illini are a better team than some of the advanced stats would suggest, largely because their defense did a 180 after a coordinator change. But the Hawkeyes are the better overall team, especially if they get decent quarterback play from Hank Brown. Iowa should control the lines of scrimmage and the general pace of the game. The only thing that could flip that is turnovers, which is something that Iowa's struggled with in losses this season. But the Hawkeyes get it done. … Iowa 27, Illinois 20.Crawford (Iowa -6.5): Can Katin Houser put the Fighting Illini in position to win this one against a defense that rarely gives up big plays? He's coming off a three-interception game against UCLA, but has been solid for the most part throughout the campaign with 18 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Iowa's playing with stakes in this one, with a chance to finish 10-2 overall by winning out. The Hawkeyes are one of six bubble teams, I'm projecting, that are battling for two at-large spots over the rest of the campaign. That matters here. ... Iowa 24, Illinois 17.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSU (-1.5) at No. 9 TennesseeHummer (LSU -1.5): It's wild to see LSU favored on the road at Tennessee given their records and season. But I agree with Vegas. I think, at least on paper, LSU is the better team. It just comes down to whether Sam Leavitt can avoid turnovers. I think after a disaster against Texas, he plays clean. Tennessee's O-line is going to struggle to dominate in the run game against LSU's defensive front. The Tigers get their first win over a ranked opponent of the Lane Kiffin era. ... LSU 24, Tennessee 20.
Crawford (Tennessee +1.5): I said last week that I would never pick Lane Kiffin to win (or cover) against a ranked team again if the Tigers burned me against Texas and it happened -- so I'm sticking with my promise. The Vols are a couple wins away from wrapping up a first-round home game, potentially more if they can find a way into the SEC Championship Game. If I'm Josh Heupel, I'd rather have an extra week of playoff prep time and let Georgia, Alabama or Texas duke it out in Atlanta ahead of the postseason. Jim Knowles finds a way to turn Sam Leavitt over and the Vols prevail. ... Tennessee 23, LSU 20.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 12 Texas Tech (-3.5) at BaylorHummer (Baylor +3.5): The Red Raiders have found something since switching to Thomas Castellanos at quarterback. They've averaged 47 points per game over the last three weeks, emerging as a dynamic run-heavy offense. Baylor matches up reasonably well defensively in this one. The Bears are a top-20 run defense and have largely contained mobile QBs this year. This game will come down to how DJ Lagway fares against a Texas Tech pass defense that's struggled this year. I think this game is close. But the Red Raiders win it late. … Texas Tech 31, Baylor 28.Crawford (Texas Tech -3.5): I took Baylor and the points last week against BYU and immediately regretted it early when the Cougars began bludgeoning the Bears at the line of scrimmage and limiting DJ Lagway's production in the passing game. Will playing at home against the Big 12's second-best team through 11 weeks alter the mentality here? Tommy Castellanos has been great for the Red Raiders over his last three starts, and I don't see that changing. ... Texas Tech 38, Baylor 31.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 Indiana (-8.5) at WashingtonHummer (Washington +8.5): This screams a trap game in Seattle. But Washington just hasn't been the program everyone expected this year. The offense continues to struggle -- the Huskies rank 125th nationally in yards per carry -- and that's not going to look any better against an elite Indiana defense. How Washington fares will depend on whether its defense, which has been solid this year, holds up against an Indiana offense that still seems stuck in the mud. This is the type of game Indiana wins ugly. … Indiana 24, Washington 17.Crawford (Indiana -8.5): Curt Cignetti needs to be careful. Politicking for his team to the CFP committee to potentially better the Hoosiers' seeding is one thing, but this isn't the same Indiana squad that was demolishing the opposition last season. They're winning with defense and just enough execution offensively to get by. He has tried to flex a schedule this season that, let's be honest, has been more than favorable for the Hoosiers. Here's another opportunity this weekend to beat a good opponent, but not a great one. ... Indiana 27, Washington 17.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 UCLA (-5.5) at MichiganHummer (Michigan +5.5): I feel like I've picked against UCLA every week this season and they keep winning games. So why stop now? These are two teams beating each other with a club. They have two elite defenses and two offenses that can struggle at times. The difference is UCLA is pretty efficient (22nd nationally in yards per play) while Michigan is anything but (124th nationally in yards per play). Still, this is the type of game the Wolverines will stay in throughout because of their defense. The offense just needs to make enough plays to keep it close. … UCLA 17, Michigan 14.
Crawford (UCLA -5.5): This is a spooky line to say the least. Every week, oddsmakers are waiting for the Bruins to catch a loss with these single-digit spreads, but it hasn't happened yet. I don't think it comes in Ann Arbor, either. If you're going to pick an outright loss for UCLA, wait until rivalry weekend against USC -- a team with a pulse and penchant for big plays offensively. There's no confidence on that side of the football for the Wolverines right now, who are going into the teeth of the best defense they've played all season. ... UCLA 20, Michigan 14.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    SMU at No. 6 Notre Dame (-20.5)Hummer (SMU +20.5): I'm not sure what happened to SMU last week against Wake Forest. But that's really representative of what the Mustangs have done all year. Notre Dame's defense ranks second nationally in yards allowed per play and should limit SMU's passing game. So whether or not the Mustangs cover comes down to their defense not repeating last week's disaster. Given that SMU has only lost two games by 20-plus points since 2023 under Rhett Lashlee, I just have a hard time seeing it happening two straight weeks. … Notre Dame 34, SMU 17.Crawford (SMU +20.5): The Mustangs are not as bad as they looked last time out. That one snowballed in a hurry against a superior opponent. Notre Dame's certainly better than SMU this season, but a second consecutive blowout for Rhett Lashlee is an unlikely outcome here. Kevin Jennings makes enough plays to keep SMU in the game before the Fighting Irish wear down the Mustangs' front seven late. ... Notre Dame 38, SMU 20.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Utah (-6.5) at TCUHummer (Utah -6.5): There's good news for TCU in this game. First, it has a top-25 defense and is good enough against the run (21st nationally) to slow down what Utah does best. They also have a top-25 passing offense, which can potentially take advantage of Utah's only real weakness in the secondary -- the Utes are 110th nationally in passing plays allowed of 20-plus yards. But I just have a hard time seeing TCU play consistently for 60 minutes in a season when turnovers and penalties have been such a big issue. This is close for a lot of the game. TCU is too good to get blown out. But the Utes make the plays down the stretch. … Utah 31, TCU 24.Crawford (Utah -6.5): What am I missing here? Utah's on a mission to grab a top-4 seed in the CFP while the Horned Frogs have altered wins and losses the last six weeks, not to mention quarterback Devon Dampier has played his way into the Heisman discussion. A multi-touchdown performance in Fort Worth to push the Utes to 11-0 could punch his ticket to New York as a Heisman finalist. Utah has scored 49 and 40 points over its last two road outings in the Big 12 and should find success in Fort Worth, too. ... Utah 35, TCU 24.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Georgia (-16.5) at No. 21 South CarolinaHummer (Georgia -16.5): I'd pick Georgia over anyone right now. LaNorris Sellers, if healthy, does present some issues for the Bulldogs. But Georgia is better everywhere. The Gamecocks will have to play clean and force turnovers on defense to stay in this game. Maybe it's close for a bit. But Georgia pulls away and wins a fourth straight game over a quality opponent by double digits. … Georgia 34, South Carolina 17.
Crawford (Georgia -16.5): I have no idea if LaNorris Sellers is going to play in this one for the Gamecocks. Even if he's listed as probable later this week, there's no telling how this South Carolina coaching staff handles his availability. The season effectively ended last week for the Gamecocks after that stunning loss at Arkansas, so I worry about the home team's focus level. Kirby Smart is 4-0 in his tenure at Georgia at Williams-Brice Stadium, which includes a couple of lopsided victories. Georgia rolls. ... Georgia 31, South Carolina 10.

title: Why Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba may go back-to-back as NFL Offensive Player of the Year - CBS Sports

body:
The league might be witnessing the greatest season ever by a wide receiver, which could earn him the first back-to-back OPOY honors in a quarter century
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:49 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Greatness is unfolding in the Pacific Northwest. Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is in the midst of a potentially legendary season — one unlike any in NFL history. A year after he blossomed into a superstar, Smith-Njigba is on pace to break the league's single-season receiving record and could become the first player to win Offensive Player of the Year in consecutive seasons since Marshall Faulk rattled off three straight award wins from 1999 to 2001.Before Faulk, only Earl Campbell (1978-1980) had achieved the rare feat of winning OPOY multiple years in a row. Both of them were running backs, so Smith-Njigba would be the first wide receiver to pull it off if he secures the trophy come February.Considering the award has only gone to a wide receiver six times since its inception in 1972, Smith-Njigba's victory last year was a rarity in the first place. To up the tally to seven wide receivers and account for two of them, in back-to-back years, would put him in a league of his own in the award's history.
Smith-Njigba leads all players this season in receptions (79), receiving yards (1,207) and receiving touchdowns (10) heading into the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. Let it not be forgotten that he is fresh off a Super Bowl title, too. At just 24 years old, he has already accomplished more at both an individual level and team level than most wide receivers dream of. As far as wideouts go, it's JSN's world, and everyone else is living in it.Single-season receiving yards record within reachWhen the Seahawks traded D.K. Metcalf in 2025, they did so clearly knowing that Smith-Njigba was ready to handle the lion's share of targets on their offense. He had already proven capable of reaching the 100-catch mark with Metcalf in the group, so the expectation was that he would take the next step as the bona fide No. 1 weapon among Seattle wide receivers. The Ohio State product did just that when he rolled to the league's receiving title in 2025.One year later, Smith-Njigba is not only on track to repeat as the NFL's most productive pass-catcher, but he is also on pace to beat Calvin Johnson's record for the most receiving yards in a single season. He does have the benefit of a 17-game season whereas Johnson played during the 16-game era, but that is not to discredit the historic heights he could reach by the end of the campaign.
Single-season receiving yards leaderboardYearPlayerRec. yards2026Jaxon Smith-Njigba's current pace2,0522012Calvin Johnson1,9642021Cooper Kupp1,9472015Julio Jones1,871Again, the breakout season Smith-Njigba strung together last year in the wake of the Metcalf trade placed him at the top of the 2025 yardage standings. Stack that season with the even greater 2026 production, and the result might end up being the best two-year run by a receiver the sport has ever seenMost receiving yards in two-year spanYearPlayerRec. yards2025-26Jaxon Smith-Njigba's current pace3,8442011-12Calvin Johnson3,6452014-15Antonio Brown3,5322022-23Tyreek Hill3,509Even if he slows down over the final seven games of the year, Smith-Njigba has already done enough through the first 10 to put himself in rare company. He became the fourth player in NFL history and the first since the 1970 merger to rack up 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns in the first 10 games of a season. The last time that occurred was 65 years ago.A 144-yard quarterIn college football, there is the "Heisman moment." Whatever the Offensive Player of the Year equivalent of that is, Smith-Njigba just had his. In the Week 10 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, he turned in the greatest quarter of his career and highlighted it with a ridiculous play that stands competitively among the best he has ever recorded.The third quarter of that triumph at Allegiant Stadium was special. Smith-Njigba amassed 144 yards and became the first Seahawk to tally 128+ receiving yards in a quarter. When he tacked on more in the next period, he entered another new echelon as the first Seattle player with 150+ receiving yards in a half in the play-by-play era, which dates back to 1991.Nearly half of his third-quarter yardage came on one single play: A 71-yard burst to the end zone.
Smith-Njigba slipped while running his route, immediately stood back up, spun past a defender, beat two safeties to a deep ball and sprinted 40 more yards to the goal line. If the slip at the start of the route was accidental, then credit to him for bouncing back to complete a monster play. If it was intentional to get the safety to bite, then it was a masterclass in baiting a defender out of position. Either way, it belongs on his career highlight reel.Two quarterbacks, one special seasonSo often in this league, when a starting quarterback goes down with an injury, his top wide receiver's production falls off a cliff. Look at what happened in Minnesota when Justin Jefferson dealt with a revolving door at quarterback, or what Zay Flowers continues to experience in Baltimore amid Lamar Jackson's absence.Smith-Njigba has actually been better with his No. 2 quarterback than with his starter.Sam Darnold has been in and out of the lineup due to multiple injuries, which thrust Drew Lock into action during the season opener, Week 2 and each of the last two games. The two longest touchdowns of Smith-Njigba's career came with Lock, not Darnold, operating the offense: last week's 71-yard explosion and an 81-yard score in the second game of the year.Here is how Smith-Njigba's production stacks up by quarterback:With Sam Darnold (6.5 games): 48 receptions, 721 yards, 5 touchdownsWith Drew Lock (3.5 games): 31 receptions, 486 yards, 5 touchdownsOpposing defenses cannot stop Smith-Njigba. Apparently, quarterback injuries can't either. He is operating in a different universe from every wide receiver in the NFL and may be recognized for it at the end of the year with another piece of hardware in his already stocked trophy case.

title: Rick Stockstill's second act: How a Florida State legend sparked turnaround - CBS Sports
description: The head coach's office inside Florida State's football facility is so large it echoes. There's a kitchen, a shower and a closet Rick St
body:
The head coach's office inside Florida State's football facility is so large it echoes. There's a kitchen, a shower and a closet Rick Stockstill swears is bigger than any house he has ever lived in.The walls have remained bare since Florida State fired Mike Norvell on Nov. 1 and named Stockstill, the former Middle Tennessee head coach, the interim head coach. A couple of Stockstill's files sit on the desk next to a Bobby Bowden bobblehead. "I look at it every day," he told CBS Sports.Stockstill hasn't moved his belongings into the spacious office, which he jokingly calls "the mansion," and he won't. He knows this might be a short-term gig."I'm not going to move twice," he said.Since taking over as interim head coach earlier this month, Stockstill has led Florida State to two consecutive victories. Both wins came on the road, ending a nearly three-year drought without a win away from Doak Campbell Stadium. Now, a team whose season appeared lost to many -- and remains so in the eyes of some -- finds itself just one win shy of bowl eligibility.
For Stockstill, the former Florida State quarterback who was part of Bowden's first full recruiting class in the 1970s, it's a dream come true. For years, he told former teammates he would love to be the Seminoles' head coach for one game, one play, one day. "It was always a dream. Well, it was a hope. I didn't think it was ever a realistic dream or realistic possibility," he said. 
        
            
                College football coaching carousel 2026: Tracking moves as Philip Rivers returns to NC State
                
                    Brandon Marcello                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
A Seminole's dream fulfilledSam Childers, a tight end who caught touchdown passes from Stockstill in 1980 and 1981, heard it plenty. "And I told him he could scratch that off his list because he's done it now," Childers said.
Now, Stockstill is the living embodiment of Florida State's bridge to the past and its future, both connected by the program's inauspicious rebuilds.Stockstill, 68, was one of Bowden's first quarterbacks, part of the foundational recruiting classes that lifted an FSU program on the cusp of abandonment to 10- and 11-win seasons. He later spent 18 years leading Middle Tennessee, his foundation built primarily on what Bowden taught him: faith, family and toughness. And players, not plays. When Stockstill was fired after the 2023 season, he reached out to his alma mater, and Norvell hired him as the program's director of offensive scouting.
Back to coaching basicsStockstill spent three years working in a cubicle, drafting scouting reports and evaluations of opponents and recruits. On game days, he reminded coaches how many timeouts they had left."Honestly, it wasn't a lot of fun. I used to tell people I like what I'm doing, but I don't love it," Stockstill said.He loves the job now. When he was installed as interim head coach, he made a few quick changes: he ordered new defensive coordinator Ernie Sims Jr. to ditch the 3-5-3 defense and install a four-man front that didn't stress the secondary as much as the previous scheme. The Seminoles, who had mostly practiced indoors, moved outside, and the loud music that played during stretching sessions was cut off so players and coaches could better communicate. Practices were shortened.
The Seminoles beat Boston College 31-24 on Nov. 7 to snap a 12-game road losing streak dating to November 2023, then edged Pittsburgh 16-10. At 5-5, they're one win from bowl eligibility, with homecoming against NC State on Saturday and a rivalry game against Florida on Nov. 27.Stockstill isn't keeping the seat warm for the next coach.  He'd love to be that coach. If not, he'd love to stay in Tallahassee as an assistant and hand the next coach a program with momentum.Building again on Bowden's foundationThat's exactly what Stockstill and his old teammates did in the late 1970s, lifting FSU into the national conversation. When Stockstill arrived in 1977 as part of Bowden's first full recruiting class, Florida State was coming off four straight losing seasons, and the administration flirted with disbanding the football program. Bowden arrived, and everything flipped. 
"We'll play anybody, anywhere, anytime, just sign the contract," Childers said, referring to Bowden's famous challenge.They did. Florida State won the Tangerine Bowl after the 1977 season and reached back-to-back Orange Bowls after the 1979 and 1980 seasons. With Stockstill at quarterback in 1980, the Seminoles beat No. 3 Nebraska in Lincoln and No. 4 Pitt at home in consecutive weeks. As a senior captain in 1981, he led them through five straight road games, winning at No. 7 Ohio State, Notre Dame and LSU.The wins piled up, but the national titles didn't come until the 1990s. Bobby's Boys, as those early classes call themselves, poured the concrete for Bowden's foundation, which held for 38 years.
Quarterback Rick Stockstill (11) led Florida State against Oklahoma in the Orange Bowl at the end of the 1980 season. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            "I'm in the building business, and you've got to have a good foundation so you can build a damn good building, right?" Childers said. "And we had a great foundation."That building is now showing cracks. Florida State went 13-0 in the 2023 regular season, won the ACC and was left out of the four-team College Football Playoff. The controversial snub sent the Seminoles barreling down a hill. They went 2-10 in 2024, the program's worst season since 1974, and 5-7 last year. Athletic director Michael Alford was fired in September, and Norvell followed less than two months later after a 3-5 start. Fans have grown tired of lagging NIL resources for players and rising debt. FSU reported $437 million in athletics debt for the 2025 fiscal year, primarily because of long-term revenue bonds tied to renovations at Doak Campbell Stadium and a new football operations building.
Brent Brock, a former Florida State offensive lineman and Stockstill's best friend since they were freshmen, doesn't believe the Seminoles have been left behind in college athletics' new NIL race."In all fairness, we haven't fallen off the edge, but we're clinging to the edge," said Brock, who played alongside Stockstill at FSU and spent 18 seasons on his staff at Middle Tennessee.Under Stockstill, Brock said, Florida State is "kind of pulling ourselves back up and trying to get back on that mountain."
Wally Woodham, a Leon High legend who shared quarterback duties with Jimmy Jordan on Bowden's first great teams from 1977 to 1979, quickly became Stockstill's running buddy when he enrolled at FSU. They've been close since. When he visited Stockstill in Tallahassee this past August, he discovered a coach sidelined to reviewing game tape and handling office paperwork, clearly dissatisfied with his inability to work directly with players."I could tell just by his demeanor and his mindset he was done," Woodham said. "... He's not an analyst. He's a football coach."Then the job came. At Boston College, trailing 17-14 with 17 seconds left before halftime, Stockstill wanted a field goal to tie the game. Offensive line coach Herb Hand asked about "Silver," a fake field goal play he installed that week. They called it, and kicker Gabe Panikowski scored on it. Walking off the field, Stockstill told the FSU radio crew what was running through his head: "I've got coach Bowden blood in me."
Pitt carried ghosts the next week. Stockstill recalled that one of his best friends, Pittsburgh native Monk Bonasorte, intercepted a pass when the Seminoles beat Dan Marino's Panthers in 1980. Bonasorte died of brain cancer in 2016. Before this year's trip, Stockstill's buddies kept texting him that Bowden and Monk were looking down on him with pride."That's why I'm so emotional," Stockstill said.The players have noticed. He cried after the first win. He also danced with the players. Childers was at a recent practice when Stockstill paused to tell the team how much he respected them."I bet I heard eight or 10 players go, 'We respect you, coach'," Childers said.The interview never stopsThe next decision is in Jeff Purinton's hands. Florida State hired Purinton, an FSU alum who spent more than a decade in the athletic department during the Bowden era, as athletic director on Nov. 9. His first full day on the job was Tuesday, and his first major assignment is hiring a football coach."I think if they walked out to that football facility right now and went into coach Stockstill's office, they could see exactly what they need," Childers said.For Bowden's Boys, they want some of what Bowden brought to the program in the next head coach. The Hall of Fame coach brought "a calmness and a steadiness," and a message, Brock said."We're going to be OK. We're not in a panic mode. Let's recruit, let's develop kids. Let's be smart about the portal."Woodham said former teammates wrote letters to the athletic director saying Stockstill deserves a shot at an interview. Stockstill doesn't know if he'll get that interview."I feel like I'm interviewing every day," Stockstill said.If Purinton goes another direction, Stockstill still wants to be a part of FSU's next chapter."Heck yeah, I'd stick around," he said. If the new coach needs a position coach, "he'll get the best one he can get right here in me. 'Cause I'll fight my guts out for him at this place."Brock called keeping Stockstill on staff "probably the easiest question I'll answer for you." Said Childers: "I wish they'd give him another year while they look for a coach."This Saturday is Homecoming against NC State. On Friday night, former players will gather at Doak Campbell Stadium, walk with the current team, and stand, one by one, to give their names, positions, and the years they lettered. Bobby's Boys will be there in force.On Saturday, Stockstill's dream will continue when he leads FSU onto the field at Doak Campbell Stadium for the first time as head coach."Having played here and my love and respect for Coach Bowden and what he meant to me in my personal and professional life, and then to be sitting in the role that he had is very humbling and just very surreal," Stockstill said. "I've cherished every second of it. I just love the opportunity and how I can impact these players and staff and the program here in a short period of time."

title: USWNT roster for Concacaf W Championship: Ashley Sanchez back, Sam Coffey returns, and Naomi Girma misses out - CBS Sports

body:
Emma Hayes names 23-player roster for Concacaf W Championship where the USWNT aim to qualify for 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup

        The biggest roster of the year for the U.S. women's national team is here. Head coach Emma Hayes has named a 23-player roster for the upcoming 2026 Concacaf W Championship. The tournament serves as the World Cup qualifiers, and four teams will earn spots in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, with future Olympic spots also in play. Fans can watch all the Concacaf W Championship matches on Paramount+.In just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round. The U.S. and Canada earned direct byes into the tournament as Concacaf's top two ranked teams, and six teams now join them after a preliminary qualifying round. The USWNT will face El Salvador on Nov. 27 in the quarterfinal round, and if they advance, they'll clinch a spot in next year's World Cup. The other matchups are Canada against Panama, Mexico vs. Haiti, and Jamaica will play Costa Rica."It's been a great year of growth and learning for our team, and for a long time the focus has been on qualifying for the World Cup, so now that time has arrived," said Hayes.
"I want to see relentless consistency from our players, individually and as a team, and I want us to be elite in both penalty boxes. If we can achieve that, I'm confident those performances will carry us through to meet our standards and goals. This is my first Concacaf event and the first for many of our players, so we're all looking forward to the experience."Hayes selected a full roster that features several players competing in their first-ever senior-level World Cup qualifying tournament, and a handful of veterans. Just eight of the 23 players selected were members of the 2022 Concacaf W Championship roster: forwards Mallory Swanson, Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson, and Ashley Sanchez; defender Emily Fox; and midfielders Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle, and Sam Coffey -- who joined mid-tournament that year.Coffey returns to the roster after missing two previous international windows while managing a lower-leg injury. Defender Naomi Girma is out as she continues to manage a lingering calf injury. The centerback has not featured with the national team since April, and has yet to play with Chelsea FC this season. Midfielder Olivia Moultrie is currently rehabbing from an ACL injury sustained in August. Other notable omissions on the roster are Jaedyn Shaw and Ally Sentnor, both of whom have been part of U23 and senior camps throughout the year.
This is just the third camp for the attacking line of "triple espresso" since the 2024 Olympics. If the trio starts a match during the Concacaf W Championship, it will be the first time they start a game together since the gold medal match. Both Swanson and Wilson have worked their way back into senior camps over the year following maternity leave. 2026 Concacaf W Championship USWNT Roster Listed by position (club; caps/goals) Goalkeepers (3): Claudia Dickey (Seattle Reign FC; 12/0), Mandy McGlynn (Utah Royals FC; 6/0), Phallon Tullis-Joyce (Manchester United, ENG; 8/0)Defenders (8): Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC; 72/3), Kate Del Fava (Utah Royals FC; 1/0), Emily Fox (Arsenal FC, ENG; 80/1), Avery Patterson (Houston Dash; 15/1), Tara Rudd (Washington Spirit; 12/0), Evelyn Shores (Angel City FC; 0/0), Gisele Thompson (Angel City FC; 12/0), Kennedy Wesley (San Diego Wave FC; 9/1)
Midfielders (6): Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current; 7/1), Sam Coffey (Manchester City, ENG; 46/5), Lindsey Heaps (Denver Summit FC; 180/40), Claire Hutton (Bay FC; 22/1), Rose Lavelle (Gotham FC; 124/29), Lily Yohannes (OL Lyonnes, FRA; 22/1)Forwards (6): Michelle Cooper (Kansas City Current; 16/1), Trinity Rodman (Washington Spirit; 59/13), Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage; 30/4), Mallory Swanson (Chicago Stars; 105/39), Alyssa Thompson (Chelsea FC, ENG; 34/4), Sophia Wilson (Portland Thorns FC; 65/25)

        The Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Royals will receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller, and lefty Jose Ferrer, in the deal, according to the Seattle Times. title: Aljamain Sterling says critics can argue with the history books as he chases more legacy: 'Numbers don't lie' - CBS Sports
description: Sterling believes a win over Kevin Vallejos at UFC Fight Night in Qatar could put him in line for a second title
body:
Sterling believes a win over Kevin Vallejos at UFC Fight Night in Qatar could put him in line for a second title shot in as many divisions
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:04 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS -- A UFC title run didn't earn Aljamain Sterling the respect it should've. Fans haven't warmly embraced him or his many accomplishments as one of the best bantamweights ever. But the "Funk Master" is stubborn and talented enough to try and achieve something that even his boldest cynics would have trouble disputing.Sterling fights Kevin Vallejos in Saturday's UFC Fight Night co-main event in Qatar. A victory could put the former bantamweight champion in line to challenge Alexander Volkanovski for the featherweight title, giving Sterling a chance to join the exclusive club of UFC fighters who have won two weight class titles. It's an opportunity the No. 4-ranked featherweight contender never expected to have this late in his career.Sterling has already accomplished more than enough to retire comfortably. He holds UFC bantamweight records for most consecutive wins and title defenses. Yet the chance to add another championship to his resume has kept him sharp. He knows better than most that winning a title doesn't always win over critics, but the numbers on his side are irrefutable."I think it's just the history books," Sterling told CBS Sports. "I have enough money where I'm more than comfortable. More money is always good, though. But I think it's just the history. That's really it. Just setting records, doing something that no one could ever take away from you."
Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC Fight Night in Qatar for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Sterling has obsessed over accolades since his amateur wrestling days, when he never achieved the championship success he wanted. That disappointment fueled his MMA career, eventually carrying him to the UFC bantamweight title and three successful defenses. Moving up to featherweight allowed him to repeat that cycle all over again."I came up short in my amateur wrestling career; I never won a national title, never got to go to the state tournament, and it just always made me hungrier to keep pushing," Sterling said. "I became a UFC champ, and after setting the records, I came up short in my last one. Then I went up to 45, and now here's a new goal. I could become a two-division champion. I think that's a special feat in itself. People can talk and say whatever they want, but numbers don't lie. So for me, that's what it's all about."
Sterling's relationship with UFC fans has been complicated since he first won the bantamweight title in 2021. Petr Yan handed him the championship after striking him with a blatantly illegal knee, resulting in a disqualification. Sterling was accused of exaggerating the damage to win a title in a fight he was clearly losing. The stink lingered even after the "Funk Master" defeated Yan in their rematch and successfully defended the championship against T.J. Dillashaw and Henry Cejudo.His reign ended just as frustratingly. Sterling faced Sean O'Malley on a quick turnaround despite dealing with injuries, losing by second-round TKO. He then moved to featherweight without a red-carpet rollout for his 135-pound accomplishments. Sterling isn't deaf to the accusations that he isn't as good as his record suggests, despite repeatedly beating fighters whom his critics hold in high regard."People still want to find a way to chip away at what I've done. Dude, look at the numbers. Clearly, I'm better than what you think," Sterling said. "I can't be that bad if I'm beating all these other guys that you rate at this level. It is what it is. I'm comfortable in my own skin. I know I've done enough. And again, for me, numbers don't lie. So if you want to say this or that, I go, 'OK, but what does it say in the history books?' So go argue with the numbers, don't argue with me."
Some fans made up their minds about Sterling the night Yan threw that illegal knee. No amount of winning will change their minds about his alleged Oscar-worthy dive. But becoming a two-division UFC champion by beating Volkanovski would make Sterling's place in MMA history much harder to dispute. He would have achieved something that many champions, including Volkanovski, never managed.Not everyone is blind to Sterling's abilities, especially those who've competed at the highest level of MMA. Volkanovski has publicly identified Sterling as the featherweight contender most deserving of a title shot, provided he beats Vallejos. It's a meaningful endorsement, given the interest in knockout artist Jean Silva as the next challenger. Recent title challenger Movsar Evloev, who narrowly defeated Sterling in December 2024, has also vouched for his former opponent. Evloev previously told CBS Sports that Silva wouldn't sniff a title shot if he had to beat Sterling first. The praise from his peers means more than criticism from those who have never set foot inside the Octagon.
"I've trained with Volk. I fought Movsar. So these guys know what they're looking at," Sterling said. "They know what they understand, see and can feel. It lets me know I'm doing something right. I'm just very fortunate, very blessed to be in this situation still."MMA suffers from short-term memory. Even Charles Oliveira and Max Holloway, beloved former champions who built legacies off thrilling performances, encountered persistent criticism after their underwhelming BMF title fight earlier this year. In team sports, many fans have an attitude of "What have you done for me lately?" It's becoming more prevalent in combat now. That can be especially damaging for a fighter when a more exciting alternative exists. In this case, the alternative is a barking Brazilian madman with dynamite in his fists.Silva is a more marketable option in some respects, with KO power that generates highlight reels and fan enthusiasm. Sterling wouldn't have accepted another dangerous opponent if he believed a title shot was in the bag. Beating Vallejos is important, but making a statement matters just as much.
Vallejos has his own ideas about Saturday's fight. The 24-year-old Argentine believes he can stifle Sterling's wrestling attacks long enough to knock him out. Sterling, whose grappling has frustrated some of the UFC's best fighters, isn't enthralled by that assessment. "If that's what he really thinks and believes, then he hasn't watched many of my fights," Sterling said. "So if that's his path to victory, as I said before, good luck. It's going to be a long night for this guy. If anything, I can make it a short one for him. So, let me get the takedown early and send you on your way home. Nice first-class ticket back home to Argentina."Even an impressive victory won't secure Sterling's immediate future. Volkanovski has expressed interest in finishing his career with a lightweight superfight against Justin Gaethje. Should Volkanovski stay put, it's possible that UFC matchmakers have already decided on Silva as the next title challenger behind closed doors. Sterling could find himself waiting or having to win again regardless of this weekend's result.
How long he's willing to pursue another title is difficult to answer. Sterling has spent almost his entire UFC career fighting ranked opponents, an unusually demanding schedule that has continued into his late 30s. Vallejos is the same age Sterling was when he signed with the promotion, and represents another generation of ambitious young fighters hoping to build their reputations at the old guard's expense."That's a hard question, man," Sterling said when asked how much longer he'd pursue a featherweight title shot. "I'm just taking it one fight at a time. See how my body does, see how I perform when I step in there with these guys. Again, these guys are so much younger than me. They're hungry. They want what I have, what I've been able to achieve. They want to make their names off of me. I understand because I was that young guy once before."I'm preparing to be the best version of myself. I go out there and do what I'm doing in the training room. It should be a beautiful night for the team, and I'll be dancing my way into a title shot opportunity."
